blocks.title: Not from your PDFs
blocks.text: No guide of yours covers this subject, so this part was written for the site, as of October 2026. Frontend libraries change quickly: check the official documentation before relying on a detail.
In a single-page app, the server sends one HTML file, and JavaScript chooses what to show based on the URL. No full reload happens when moving between pages.

blocks.title: Routes with React Router

blocks.text: ### Reading the URL

blocks.title: Hooks for route data

blocks.text:
### The 404 on refresh

A very common deployment bug. The user opens `/orders/42`, which works through client routing. But on refresh, the browser asks the **server** for `/orders/42`, and no such file exists.

blocks.code:
sequenceDiagram
  participant B as Browser
  participant S as Server or CDN
  B->>S: GET /orders/42
  S-->>B: 404, as there's no such file
  Note over B,S: Fix: serve index.html for unknown paths, and let React Router handle it
  B->>S: GET /orders/42
  S-->>B: index.html
  B->>B: Router shows the order page
blocks.title: Why refresh gives a 404

blocks.text: The fix is to send `index.html` for any path that's not a real file. In Spring Boot, forward non-API routes. In CloudFront, map 403 and 404 errors to `/index.html`, though that also hides API 404s if they share the same distribution, so scope this behaviour carefully. Nginx uses `try_files $uri /index.html`.

blocks.title: Serving a React build from Spring Boot

blocks.text: ### Protecting routes

blocks.title: A guard component

blocks.text: Anyone can change JavaScript in their browser. A route guard only improves the experience. Your Spring Boot API must check permissions on every request.
blocks.title: Guards aren't security

blocks.text:
### Data routers

Route **loaders** fetch before showing a page, and **actions** handle form submissions. They reduce loading flicker, and work with TanStack Query as well.

blocks.title: Loaders and error handling

blocks.text:
### Split per route

Loading each page lazily keeps the first download small: routes are the natural points to split, as Part 9 shows. Also restore scroll position (`<ScrollRestoration />`) and update the page title, so that navigation feels normal.

blocks.title: Key points
blocks.text:
- Client routing needs a server fallback
- Guards are for experience, not security
- Put view state in the URL
- Split code by route

For simple forms, let the browser hold values, and read them on submit.

### React Hook Form with Zod

For real forms, with many fields, validation and server errors, use a library. It avoids re-rendering on every keystroke, and removes much repetitive code.

blocks.title: A typed, validated form

blocks.text:
`z.coerce` changes the type between input and output, which is why this form names both. Using a single `z.infer` type here gives a compile error, so copy this shape when any field is coerced or transformed.

### Matching validation with Spring Boot

Validation runs twice: the client gives fast feedback, while the server is what counts. Map Spring's errors onto fields.

blocks.title: Field errors in a shape React can use

blocks.text:
### Form details that matter

| Detail | Why |
|---|---|
| Disable submit while pending | Prevents duplicates; the server should still be idempotent |
| Show errors next to fields | Faster to fix |
| Keep input after an error | Don't punish people by clearing it |
| Warn before losing changes | Long forms |
| Correct input types and autocomplete | Mobile keyboards, password managers |
| Validate on blur or submit, not on each key | Less noise |

### File uploads

blocks.title: Upload with progress

blocks.text: Your AWS part explains pre-signed URLs. Check size and type in the browser for quick feedback, and again on the server, where it counts.

blocks.title: Key points
blocks.text:
- Use FormData for simple forms
- Use a form library with a schema for real ones
- Validate on both sides
- Map server errors onto fields
### Nested routes share layouts

blocks.title: An account area with tabs that keep their layout

blocks.code:
flowchart TD
  A["/account/orders/42"] --> B[AppLayout: Outlet]
  B --> C[AccountLayout: Outlet]
  C --> D[OrderDetails]
blocks.title: How nested routes render

blocks.text:
`NavLink` knows if it matches the URL, and it sets `aria-current="page"` and an active class. Moving between tabs renders only what changes, so that scroll, layout and state in the parent survive. A nested `errorElement` means that a failure replaces only that part of the screen.

### Loaders and actions

A **loader** runs before a route renders, and an **action** handles a form submission.

blocks.title: A route with data and a mutation

blocks.text:
After an action, the router automatically reloads the page's loaders, so that data stays fresh without manual cache work.

| Approach | Good | Watch out |
|---|---|---|
| TanStack Query in components | Rich cache; simple to adopt | Loading happens after navigation |
| Router loaders | No loading flicker; data before render | Basic caching on its own |
| Both | Loader calls `ensureQueryData` | A little more setup |

### Unsaved changes

blocks.title: Warn before leaving

blocks.text:
`useBlocker` needs a data router, and it covers navigation inside your app. `beforeunload` covers leaving the app.

### URL design

| Rule | Good | Avoid |
|---|---|---|
| Resource in the path | `/orders/42` | `/orderDetails?id=42` |
| View state in query | `/orders?status=PAID&page=2` | State in memory only |
| Nouns | `/orders` | `/getOrders` |
| Readable | `/products/java-book-42` | `/p?x=42&y=a7` |

Validate values in the URL, as users can type anything: `?page=abc` shouldn't crash the page.

blocks.title: Key points
blocks.text:
- Layouts nest through Outlet
- Nested errorElement limits damage
- Actions reload loaders
- Validate URL values

blocks.text:
### Dynamic rows with useFieldArray

An invoice has any number of line items, each validated.

blocks.title: An invoice form

blocks.text:
Use `field.id` as the key, never the array index, as `useFieldArray` provides it for this reason. Both add and remove buttons have `type="button"`, otherwise they'd submit the form. Note that `total` here is for display only: the server must calculate the real total.

blocks.text:
### Editing existing data

Load the data first, then pass it as default values. Remount with a `key`, or call `reset(data)`, when the data arrives.

blocks.title: Edit form

blocks.text:
Consider what happens if two people edit one record. Send a version with the form, and let Spring's `@Version` return a 409, which the UI can explain.

### Non-native inputs

Date pickers and custom selects don't expose a `ref` to a real input, so use `Controller`.

blocks.title: Controller adapts a custom component

blocks.text:
### Accessible forms

| Practice | Why |
|---|---|
| Move focus to the first error on submit | Keyboard and screen reader users find it |
| `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby` | Links errors to fields |
| `fieldset` and `legend` for groups | Gives context to radio groups |
| Don't rely on placeholders or colour | Both can be missed |
| Don't disable submit until valid | People can't discover what's wrong |

React Hook Form focuses the first invalid field by default, using registered refs.

blocks.title: Key points
blocks.text:
- Use field.id as the key
- Type="button" for non-submit buttons
- Use path to place cross-field errors
- Controller adapts custom inputs
#### Client-side routing

items.question: A deployed app works until a user refreshes on /orders/42. Why?
items.answer: The server has no such file. Serve index.html for app paths, and let the router handle them.

items.question: Why isn't a RequireAuth component enough to protect admin data?
items.answer: Client code can be changed by the user. The API must check permissions.

blocks.text: #### Forms from simple to serious

items.question: Why does React Hook Form re-render less than controlled inputs?
items.answer: It keeps inputs uncontrolled and reads values through refs, so typing needn't render the form.

items.question: The server returns a 400 for a duplicate email. How should the UI show it?
items.answer: Map it to the email field's error, and keep the user's other input.

items.question: Why disable the submit button if the server is idempotent anyway?
items.answer: It gives clear feedback and avoids needless requests. The server's protection remains the real guarantee.

blocks.text: #### Nested layouts, loaders and actions

items.question: What does Outlet do?
items.answer: It marks where the matched child route renders in a parent layout.

items.question: How do you warn about closing a tab with unsaved work?
items.answer: A `beforeunload` listener, while dirty. Use `useBlocker` for navigation inside the app.

items.question: A user changes ?page=abc in the URL. What should happen?
items.answer: Parse and validate it, then fall back to page 1, rather than crashing or sending it to the API.

blocks.text: #### Hard forms: arrays, dependent fields and editing

items.question: Why not use the array index as key in useFieldArray?
items.answer: Removing a row would shift indexes, and inputs would keep the wrong values. `field.id` is stable.

items.question: How does a cross-field error appear on the right input?
items.answer: The refine's `path` names the field that receives it.

items.question: Two people edit one order. How can the second be told?
items.answer: Send a version, let Spring's `@Version` return a 409, and offer to reload.
